claim: Transplantation of MHC compatible, minor antigen mismatched bone marrow stromal/stem cells (BMSCs) play a role in the pathogenesis of fibrosis in a scleroderma mouse model.
source: Using a scleroderma mouse, we show that transplantation of MHC compatible, minor antigen mismatched bone marrow stromal/stem cells (BMSCs) play a role in the pathogenesis of fibrosis.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding based on the experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Removal of donor BMSCs rescued mice from disease.
source: Removal of donor BMSCs rescued mice from disease.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1Bv and related panels.

claim: Freshly isolated PDGFRα+ Sca-1+ BMSCs expressed MHC class II following transplantation.
source: Freshly isolated PDGFRα+ Sca-1+ BMSCs expressed MHC class II following transplantation and activated host T cells.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6F and Figure 7B.

claim: Freshly isolated PDGFRα+ Sca-1+ BMSCs activated host T cells following transplantation.
source: Freshly isolated PDGFRα+ Sca-1+ BMSCs expressed MHC class II following transplantation and activated host T cells.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by proliferation assays and IL-6 production data in Figure 6A and 6B.

claim: A decrease in FOXP3+ CD25+ Treg population was observed following mismatched BMSC transplantation.
source: A decrease in FOXP3+ CD25+ Treg population was observed.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7C and 7D.

claim: T cells proliferated when stimulated with mismatched BMSCs in vitro.
source: T cells proliferated and secreted IL-6 when stimulated with mismatched BMSCs in vitro.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by BrdU proliferation assay data in Figure 6A.

claim: T cells secreted IL-6 when stimulated with mismatched BMSCs in vitro.
source: T cells proliferated and secreted IL-6 when stimulated with mismatched BMSCs in vitro.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by ELISA data in Figure 6B.

claim: Donor T cells were not involved in fibrosis because transplanting T cell-deficient RAG2 knock out mice bone marrow still caused disease.
source: Donor T cells were not involved in fibrosis because transplanting T cell-deficient RAG2 knock out mice bone marrow still caused disease.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by histological data in Figure 3B and HSP47+ cell counts in Figure 3C.

claim: Once initially triggered by mismatched BMSCs, the autoimmune phenotype was not donor BMSC dependent as the phenotype was observed after effector T cells were adoptively transferred into naïve syngeneic mice.
source: Once initially triggered by mismatched BMSCs, the autoimmune phenotype was not donor BMSC dependent as the phenotype was observed after effector T cells were adoptively transferred into naïve syngeneic mice.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by adoptive transfer experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Minor antigen mismatched BMSCs trigger systemic fibrosis in this autoimmune scleroderma model.
source: Our data suggest that minor antigen mismatched BMSCs trigger systemic fibrosis in this autoimmune scleroderma model.
evidence: The abstract concludes with this interpretation based on the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The bone marrow transplantation model using B10.D2 donor mice and BALB/c recipient mice is a MHC-compatible, minor histocompatibility antigen (miHA)–incompatible model of systemic fibrosis.
source: A known bone marrow transplantation (BMT) model using 8-week-old donor B10.D2 (H-2d) mice and recipient BALB/c mice (H-2d), is a MHC-compatible, minor histocompatibility antigen (miHA)–incompatible model of systemic fibrosis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Zhang et al., 2002).
evidence: The text cites Zhang et al., 2002 as the source of this established model.

claim: Signs of fibrosis appear by 3 weeks after BMT in the scleroderma mouse model.
source: Signs of fibrosis appear by 3 weeks after BMT and progresses to a full-blown disease by 8 weeks characterized by excessive fibrosis of the lacrimal gland, conjunctiva, salivary gland, skin, lung, liver, and intestine (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The text describes the timeline of disease progression, supported by histological images in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Fibrosis progresses to a full-blown disease by 8 weeks after BMT characterized by excessive fibrosis of the lacrimal gland, conjunctiva, salivary gland, skin, lung, liver, and intestine.
source: Signs of fibrosis appear by 3 weeks after BMT and progresses to a full-blown disease by 8 weeks characterized by excessive fibrosis of the lacrimal gland, conjunctiva, salivary gland, skin, lung, liver, and intestine (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The text describes the disease progression with specific organ involvement, supported by histological images.

claim: PαS-BMSCs express CD29, CD90, and CD106, known as established markers of BMSCs.
source: We confirmed that PαS BMSCs cells expressed CD29, CD90, and CD106, known as established markers of BMSCs.
evidence: The text states this characterization, supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: CD31 and CD133, markers of endothelial cells, consisted of only a small portion of the PαS BMSCs fraction.
source: However, CD31 and CD133, markers of endothelial cells, consisted of only a small portion of the PαS BMSCs fraction (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The text describes the characterization of PαS-BMSCs, supported by flow cytometry data.

claim: Progressive fibrosis was only observed in mice receiving mismatched BMSCs.
source: Notably, progressive fibrosis was only observed in mice receiving mismatched BMSCs (Figure 1Bii,iv and Figure 1—figure supplement 3Aii,iv).
evidence: The text states this finding, supported by histological images showing fibrosis in specific transplant groups.

claim: Recipients of mismatched HSCs combined with syngeneic BMSCs were indistinguishable from syngeneic HSC and syngeneic BMSC recipients.
source: The recipients of mismatched HSCs combined with syngeneic BMSCs were indistinguishable from syngeneic HSC and syngeneic BMSC recipients.
evidence: The text describes this observation, supported by histological data in Figure 1Bi,iii.

claim: Heat-shock protein 47 (HSP47) is a molecular chaperon specific to collagen-secreting cells.
source: Since heat-shock protein 47 (HSP47), a molecular chaperon specific to collagen-secreting cells, has been reported as a useful marker for fibroblasts in paraffin-embedded tissue sections (Kuroda and Tajima, 2004), we determined the state of fibrosis by (1) semi-quantitative analysis to count the number of HSP47+ fibroblasts per field and (2) Mallory staining, a specific marker of connective tissue (Figure 1B,C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B) (Brack et al., 2007).
evidence: The text cites Kuroda and Tajima, 2004 as the source for this characterization of HSP47.

claim: HSP47 has been reported as a useful marker for fibroblasts in paraffin-embedded tissue sections.
source: Since heat-shock protein 47 (HSP47), a molecular chaperon specific to collagen-secreting cells, has been reported as a useful marker for fibroblasts in paraffin-embedded tissue sections (Kuroda and Tajima, 2004), we determined the state of fibrosis by (1) semi-quantitative analysis to count the number of HSP47+ fibroblasts per field and (2) Mallory staining, a specific marker of connective tissue (Figure 1B,C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,B) (Brack et al., 2007).
evidence: The text cites Kuroda and Tajima, 2004 as the source for this application of HSP47.

claim: Fibrotic lesions in mismatched BMSC recipients had significantly higher HSP47+ fibroblasts.
source: Fibrotic lesions in mismatched BMSC recipients had significantly higher HSP47+ fibroblasts (Figure 1C).
evidence: The text states this finding, supported by quantitative data in Figure 1C.

claim: Lacrimal gland function was reduced only in mismatched BMSC recipients.
source: Lacrimal gland function was also reduced only in mismatched BMSC recipients (Figure 1D).
evidence: The text states this finding, supported by tear volume measurements in Figure 1D.

claim: BMSC-depleted WBM transplantation canceled the fibrotic observations.
source: In addition, all these observations were canceled in recipients of BMSC-depleted WBM transplantation (Figure 1Bv,Cv,Dv and Figure 1—figure supplement 3Av,Bv).
evidence: The text states this finding, supported by histological and functional data in multiple figure panels.

claim: The severity of fibrosis triggered by mismatched BMSCs was dose dependent on the number of transplanted BMSCs.
source: The severity of fibrosis triggered by mismatched BMSCs was dose dependent on the number of transplanted BMSCs (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: The text states this finding, supported by dose-response data in Figure 1E,F.

claim: Approximately 42.9 ± 7.3% of the HSP47+ cells in fibrotic tissue were GFP+ donor-derived when mismatched EGFP+B10.D2 PαS-BMSCs were transplanted.
source: Approximately 42.9 ± 7.3% of the HSP47+ cells in fibrotic tissue were GFP+, indicating that the majority of fibroblasts were derived from donor PαS-BMSCs (Figure 2A).
evidence: The text provides quantitative data from immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The majority of fibroblasts in fibrotic tissue were derived from donor PαS-BMSCs.
source: Approximately 42.9 ± 7.3% of the HSP47+ cells in fibrotic tissue were GFP+, indicating that the majority of fibroblasts were derived from donor PαS-BMSCs (Figure 2A).
evidence: The text interprets the quantitative data as indicating donor BMSC origin of fibroblasts.

claim: Cells derived from mismatched donor EGF+SP-HSCs migrated to fibrotic lesions but none of the GFP+ cells expressed HSP47.
source: On the other hand, a notable number of cells derived from mismatched donor EGF+SP-HSCs also migrated to fibrotic lesions, but none of the GFP+ cells expressed HSP47 (Figure 2B).
evidence: The text describes this observation from immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The lineage exclusivity of the transplantation excludes the possibility that HSP47+ fibroblasts were derived from SP-HSCs.
source: The lineage exclusivity of this transplantation excludes the possibility that HSP47+ fibroblasts were derived from SP-HSCs as shown in our previous report (Koide et al., 2007).
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the experimental design and cites a previous report.

claim: The accumulation of donor-derived fibroblasts was not observed in syngeneic transplantation, where fibrosis does not occur.
source: The accumulation of donor-derived fibroblasts was not observed in syngeneic transplantation, where fibrosis does not occur (Figure 2C).
evidence: The text states this observation, supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2C.

claim: Mismatched BMSCs migrate into the target organs and proliferate under pathological microenvironment.
source: These results suggest that mismatched BMSCs migrate into the target organs and proliferate under pathological microenvironment.
evidence: The text interprets the experimental results to suggest this mechanism.

claim: The majority of fibroblasts from lacrimal gland cultures were derived from mismatched EGFP+ BMSC.
source: In vitro culture also confirmed that the majority of fibroblasts from lacrimal gland cultures were derived from mismatched EGFP+ BMSC (Figure 2D, right), whereas no EGFP+ fibroblasts were observed after mismatched EGFP+ HSC transplantation (Figure 2D, left).
evidence: The text describes this finding from in vitro culture experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claim: No EGFP+ fibroblasts were observed in lacrimal gland cultures after mismatched EGFP+ HSC transplantation.
source: In vitro culture also confirmed that the majority of fibroblasts from lacrimal gland cultures were derived from mismatched EGFP+ BMSC (Figure 2D, right), whereas no EGFP+ fibroblasts were observed after mismatched EGFP+ HSC transplantation (Figure 2D, left).
evidence: The text describes this observation from in vitro culture experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The migration of donor-derived fibroblasts to peripheral organs is one of the characteristic phenomena associated with pathogenesis or progression of this disease.
source: This suggests that the migration of donor-derived fibroblasts to peripheral organs is one of the characteristic phenomena associated with pathogenesis or progression of this disease.
evidence: The text interprets the experimental observations to suggest this characteristic of the disease.

claim: The progression of fibrosis in this mouse model is T-cell-dependent.
source: The progression of fibrosis in this mouse model is T-cell-dependent as evidenced by the fact that fibrosis was not observed when BALB/c-nu/nu mice were used as recipients of mismatched B10.D2 BMSCs transplantation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on experiments using T-cell-deficient nude mice shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Fibrosis was not observed when BALB/c-nu/nu mice were used as recipients of mismatched B10.D2 BMSCs transplantation.
source: The progression of fibrosis in this mouse model is T-cell-dependent as evidenced by the fact that fibrosis was not observed when BALB/c-nu/nu mice were used as recipients of mismatched B10.D2 BMSCs transplantation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The text describes this experimental result shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both host-derived T cells and donor HSC-derived T cells are believed to exist in this mouse model.
source: Both host-derived T cells and donor HSC-derived T cells are believed to exist in this mouse model, because mature T cells often escape radiation damage and remain in the peripheral blood of recipients (Anderson et al., 2004).
evidence: The text states this belief based on known biology of T cells after irradiation, citing Anderson et al., 2004.

claim: Mature T cells often escape radiation damage and remain in the peripheral blood of recipients.
source: Both host-derived T cells and donor HSC-derived T cells are believed to exist in this mouse model, because mature T cells often escape radiation damage and remain in the peripheral blood of recipients (Anderson et al., 2004).
evidence: The text cites Anderson et al., 2004 as the source for this biological phenomenon.

claim: Almost all spleen cells were donor-derived in matched WBMT.
source: Interestingly, almost all spleen cells were donor-derived in matched WBMT, whereas the remaining host-derived cells after mismatched WBMT were higher in mismatched WBMT (Figure 2E).
evidence: The text describes this observation from GFP analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The remaining host-derived cells after mismatched WBMT were higher in mismatched WBMT compared to matched WBMT.
source: Interestingly, almost all spleen cells were donor-derived in matched WBMT, whereas the remaining host-derived cells after mismatched WBMT were higher in mismatched WBMT (Figure 2E).
evidence: The text describes this observation from GFP analysis shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Fibrosis was not observed when BALB/c-RAG2KO mice lacking recipient T cells were used as recipients.
source: To determine the origin of T cells, we used BALB/c-RAG2KO mice as recipients or donors of HSCs. In the former lacking recipient T cells (Figure 3A), the fibrosis was not observed (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: The text describes this experimental result shown in Figure 3A,C.

claim: Donor RAG2KO HSCs lacking T cells combined with mismatched BMSCs induced fibrosis with increased HSP47+ fibroblasts in wild-type BALB/c recipients.
source: However, donor RAG2KO HSCs lacking T cells combined with mismatched BMSCs in the latter (Figure 3B) induced fibrosis with increased HSP47+ fibroblasts in wild-type BALB/c recipients (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: The text describes this experimental result shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: Recipient-derived Th 17 cells were in proximity of donor-derived BMSCs in the lacrimal gland at 8 weeks after mismatched BMSC transplantation.
source: In addition, we found that recipient-derived Th 17 cells were in proximity of donor-derived BMSCs (Figure 4A, left) and that donor BMSCs produce IL-6 (Figure 4B, left) around the ducts of the lacrimal gland in BALB/c recipient mice at 8 weeks after mismatched BMSC transplantation.
evidence: The text describes this observation from immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Donor BMSCs produce IL-6 around the ducts of the lacrimal gland in BALB/c recipient mice at 8 weeks after mismatched BMSC transplantation.
source: In addition, we found that recipient-derived Th 17 cells were in proximity of donor-derived BMSCs (Figure 4A, left) and that donor BMSCs produce IL-6 (Figure 4B, left) around the ducts of the lacrimal gland in BALB/c recipient mice at 8 weeks after mismatched BMSC transplantation.
evidence: The text describes this observation from immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Mismatched donor HSC did not produce Th 17 cells or IL-6.
source: In comparison, mismatched donor HSC did not produce Th 17 cells (Figure 4A, right) or IL-6 (Figure 4B, right).
evidence: The text describes this observation from immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: CD4+IL-17+ cells comprised more than 50% of splenic cells from B10.D2 BMSC + RAG2KO HSCs transplanted BALB/c recipients.
source: In spleen cells, flow cytometric analysis revealed a significant increase of recipient-derived CD4+Th 17 cells when donor BMSCs with RAG2KO HSCs were transplanted into BALB/c recipients (Figure 4C, Left).
evidence: The text describes this finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: CD4+Th 17 cells were scarcely detected when donor BMSCs with wild-type BALB/c HSCs were transplanted into RAG2KO recipient.
source: In contrast, CD4+Th 17 cells were scarcely detected when donor BMSCs with wild-type BALB/c HSCs were transplanted into RAG2KO recipient (Figure 4C, Right).
evidence: The text describes this observation from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Adoptive transfer of splenic T cells from mismatched BMSC-transplanted recipient into naive nude mice induced primary inflammation and following fibrosis in target organs.
source: To further confirm the function of mismatched PαS-BMSC-transplanted recipient-derived T cells, we adoptively transferred splenic T cells from mismatched BMSC-transplanted recipient into naive nude mice (BALB/c background). We found the primary inflammation and following fibrosis occurred in the target organs including the lacrimal glands, salivary glands, skin, lung, liver, and intestine (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The text describes this experimental result from adoptive transfer experiments shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The number of HSP47+ fibroblasts per field was significantly increased in the adoptively transferred nude mice compared with the wild-type control.
source: The number of HSP47+ fibroblasts per field was significantly increased in the adoptively transferred nude mice (Figure 5B) compared with the wild-type control.
evidence: The text describes this quantitative finding shown in Figure 5B.

claim: CD4+Th 17 cells were markedly elevated in splenic PBMC of the adoptive transferred recipients compared to wild-type BALB/c background nude mice.
source: Splenic PBMC of the adoptive transferred recipients revealed that CD4+Th 17 cells were markedly elevated (Figure 5C, Left) compared to the wild-type BALB/c background nude mice (Figure 5C, Right).
evidence: The text describes this finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: IL-17 concentration significantly increased in the serum from the adoptive transferred recipients group compared with the control group.
source: We conducted IL-17 ELISA using the serum samples from the same mice of the experiments shown in Figure 4C. IL-17 concentration significantly increased in the serum from the adoptive transferred recipients group compared with the control group (Figure 5D).
evidence: The text describes this finding from ELISA analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Recipient mature T cells act as an effector for mismatched PαS-BMSCs during the onset of fibrosis.
source: These results strongly suggest that recipient mature T cells act as an effector for mismatched PαS-BMSCs during the onset of fibrosis.
evidence: The text interprets the experimental results to suggest this mechanism.

claim: It is unlikely that escape of donor-derived T cells from negative selection by the host thymus is involved in the recognition of host tissue as non-self.
source: Since EGFP+ BMSC-derived cells were not observed in the cortical region of the thymus within this time frame (data not shown), it is unlikely that escape of donor-derived T cells from negative selection by the host thymus is involved in the recognition of host tissue as non-self.
evidence: The text states this conclusion based on the absence of EGFP+ BMSC-derived cells in the thymus.

claim: T cells derived from mismatched BMSC-transplanted recipients proliferated in response to PαS-BMSCs but not DCs.
source: To confirm that mature host T cells react to mismatched BMSCs, Thy-1+ T cells from various recipients (mismatched BMSC-transplanted, syngeneic BMSC-transplanted, untreated B10.D2 or untreated BALB/c mice) were co-cultured with freshly isolated PαS-BMSCs or splenic dendritic cells (DCs) from BALB/c or B10.D2 mice. T cells derived from mismatched BMSC-transplanted recipients proliferated and produced IL-6 in response to PαS-BMSCs but not DCs (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: The text describes this finding from co-culture experiments shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: T cells derived from mismatched BMSC-transplanted recipients produced IL-6 in response to PαS-BMSCs but not DCs.
source: To confirm that mature host T cells react to mismatched BMSCs, Thy-1+ T cells from various recipients (mismatched BMSC-transplanted, syngeneic BMSC-transplanted, untreated B10.D2 or untreated BALB/c mice) were co-cultured with freshly isolated PαS-BMSCs or splenic dendritic cells (DCs) from BALB/c or B10.D2 mice. T cells derived from mismatched BMSC-transplanted recipients proliferated and produced IL-6 in response to PαS-BMSCs but not DCs (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: The text describes this finding from co-culture experiments shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: T cells from mismatched BMSC-transplanted recipients also responded to matched (BALB/c) BMSCs.
source: Interestingly, T cells also responded to matched (BALB/c) BMSCs (Figure 6A,B), suggesting that recipient T cells acquired the auto-reactive nature via antigen spreading (Shlomchik, 2007).
evidence: The text describes this observation from co-culture experiments shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: Recipient T cells acquired the auto-reactive nature via antigen spreading.
source: Interestingly, T cells also responded to matched (BALB/c) BMSCs (Figure 6A,B), suggesting that recipient T cells acquired the auto-reactive nature via antigen spreading (Shlomchik, 2007).
evidence: The text interprets the experimental observation and cites Shlomchik, 2007 for the concept of antigen spreading.

claim: Either strain-derived BMSCs induced slight IL-6 secretion when reacted with naive T cells from wild-type mice.
source: In addition, either strain-derived BMSCs induced slight IL-6 secretion when reacted with naive T cells from wild-type mice (Figure 6B).
evidence: The text describes this observation from co-culture experiments shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Both PαS-BMSCs and T cells from mismatched BMSC-transplanted recipients produce IL-6.
source: Both PαS-BMSCs and T cells from mismatched BMSC-transplanted recipients produce IL-6 (Figure 6C).
evidence: The text describes this finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The T cell proliferation reaction was significantly suppressed by anti-MHC-class II antibody.
source: Since the reaction was significantly suppressed by anti-MHC-class II antibody (Figure 6D) and CD4+ T cells were predominant over CD8+ T cells (Figure 6E), it was suggested that PαS-BMSCs themselves act as antigen-presenting cells via MHC-class II.
evidence: The text describes this finding from antibody blocking experiments shown in Figure 6D.

claim: CD4+ T cells were predominant over CD8+ T cells in the proliferation response.
source: Since the reaction was significantly suppressed by anti-MHC-class II antibody (Figure 6D) and CD4+ T cells were predominant over CD8+ T cells (Figure 6E), it was suggested that PαS-BMSCs themselves act as antigen-presenting cells via MHC-class II.
evidence: The text describes this finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: PαS-BMSCs themselves act as antigen-presenting cells via MHC-class II.
source: Since the reaction was significantly suppressed by anti-MHC-class II antibody (Figure 6D) and CD4+ T cells were predominant over CD8+ T cells (Figure 6E), it was suggested that PαS-BMSCs themselves act as antigen-presenting cells via MHC-class II.
evidence: The text interprets the experimental results to suggest this mechanism.

claim: MHC-class II molecule was expressed in only a rare subset of PαS cells before co-culture.
source: Flowcytometry also revealed that MHC-class II molecule was expressed in only a rare subset of PαS cells, but the frequency of MHC-class II expressing cells was significantly increased after co-culture with recipient T cells (Figure 6F).
evidence: The text describes this finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The frequency of MHC-class II expressing cells was significantly increased after co-culture with recipient T cells.
source: Flowcytometry also revealed that MHC-class II molecule was expressed in only a rare subset of PαS cells, but the frequency of MHC-class II expressing cells was significantly increased after co-culture with recipient T cells (Figure 6F).
evidence: The text describes this finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Mismatched BMSCs and host T cells stimulate each other via unknown but specific antigens expressed in mismatched BMSCs, but not in DCs, presented by MHC class II molecules.
source: These data suggest that mismatched BMSCs and host T cells stimulate each other via unknown but specific antigens expressed in mismatched BMSCs, but not in DCs, presented by MHC class II molecules.
evidence: The text interprets the experimental data to suggest this mechanism.

claim: Serum levels of IL-6 increased in recipient mice transplanted with mismatched BMSCs starting at 3 weeks after transplantation.
source: We further examined the in vivodynamics of T cells and BMSCs. We found that serum levels of IL-6 increased in recipient mice transplanted with mismatched BMSCs starting at 3 weeks after transplantation (Figure 7A).
evidence: The text describes this finding from ELISA analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claim: PαS-BMSC-derived cells appeared in the peripheral blood of recipients starting at 3 weeks after transplantation and gradually increasing up to 7 weeks.
source: This coincided with the appearance of PαS-BMSC-derived cells in the peripheral blood of recipients starting at 3 weeks after transplantation and gradually increasing up to 7 weeks (Figure 7B).
evidence: The text describes this finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Significant number of the PαS-BMSC-derived cells in the peripheral blood expressed MHC class II antigens after transplantation.
source: Interestingly, significant number of the PαS-BMSC-derived cells in the peripheral blood expressed MHC class II antigens, whereas the vast majority of them were negative prior to transplantation (Figure 6F,7B).
evidence: The text describes this finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 6F and 7B.

claim: Increased IL-6 during an autoimmune process leads to the induction of Th17 cells and a decrease in regulatory T cells (Tregs).
source: Increased IL-6 during an autoimmune process leads to the induction of Th17 cells and a decrease in regulatory T cells (Tregs) (Bettelli et al., 2006).
evidence: The text cites Bettelli et al., 2006 as the source for this biological mechanism.

claim: CD4+CD25+Foxp3+ Tregs in peripheral blood transiently increased following lethal irradiation after syngeneic transplantation of BMSCs or WBM.
source: We found that CD4+CD25+Foxp3+ Tregs in peripheral blood transiently increased following lethal irradiation after syngeneic transplantation of BMSCs or WBM, which recovered to basal levels by 8 weeks.
evidence: The text describes this finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The transient increase in Tregs reached statistical significance at 3 weeks after syngeneic transplantation.
source: This transient increase in Tregs, reaching statistical significance at 3 weeks, was not observed after mismatched BMSC or WBM transplantation (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: The text describes this finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 7C,D.

claim: The transient increase in Tregs was not observed after mismatched BMSC or WBM transplantation.
source: This transient increase in Tregs, reaching statistical significance at 3 weeks, was not observed after mismatched BMSC or WBM transplantation (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: The text describes this finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 7C,D.

claim: An increase of Th17 cells was observed in both the mismatched WBMT and BMSC groups reaching statistical significance compared to syngeneic controls.
source: This was followed by an increase of Th17 cells in both the mismatched WBMT and BMSC groups reaching statistical significance compared to syngeneic controls at 3 weeks in the WBMT group, and 8 weeks in the BMSC mismatched group.
evidence: The text describes this finding from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 7E,F.

claim: Mismatched BMT more rapidly induces the appearance of CD4+/Th17+ cells compared with mismatched PαS cells.
source: Mismatched BMT more rapidly induces the appearance of CD4+/Th17+ cells compared with mismatched PαS cells. (Figure 7E,F).
evidence: The text describes this observation from flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 7E,F.

claim: The interaction of mismatched BMSCs and recipient T cells induce IL-6 production and lead to pathological changes in major organs similar to autoimmune disease.
source: These results suggest that the interaction of mismatched BMSCs and recipient T cells induce IL-6 production and lead to pathological changes in major organs similar to autoimmune disease, with inflammation due to Th17 cells via suppression of transient increase in Tregs.
evidence: The text interprets the experimental results to suggest this mechanism.

claim: Depletion of BMSCs from donor whole bone marrow significantly reduced fibrosis in all organs examined.
source: Our data show that depletion of BMSCs from donor whole bone marrow significantly reduced fibrosis in all organs examined, and rescued mice from lacrimal gland dysfunction associated with the disease.
evidence: The text summarizes this finding from the experimental data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Depletion of BMSCs from donor whole bone marrow rescued mice from lacrimal gland dysfunction associated with the disease.
source: Our data show that depletion of BMSCs from donor whole bone marrow significantly reduced fibrosis in all organs examined, and rescued mice from lacrimal gland dysfunction associated with the disease.
evidence: The text summarizes this finding from the experimental data presented in Figure 1D.

claim: The number of BMSCs in graft correlated with severity of fibrosis.
source: These findings suggest the possible role of donor BMSCs in the initiation of the autoimmune process, as the number of BMSCs in graft correlated with severity of fibrosis (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: The text states this correlation based on dose-response data shown in Figure 1E,F.

claim: The onset of true autoimmune disease in these mice was shown by the repression of Treg induction, followed by an increase in Th17 effector cells of host origin.
source: Furthermore, the onset of true autoimmune disease in these mice was shown by the repression of Treg induction, followed by an increase in Th17 effector cells of host origin.
evidence: The text summarizes this finding from the experimental data presented in Figure 7.

claim: Migrating donor PαS-BMSCs are the initial trigger of events leading to increased levels of circulating IL-6, followed by a decrease in Tregs, and conversely an increase in host-derived Th17 cells.
source: This shows that migrating donor PαS-BMSCs are the initial trigger of events leading to increased levels of circulating IL-6, followed by a decrease in Tregs, and conversely an increase in host-derived Th17 cells.
evidence: The text interprets the experimental results to propose this sequence of events.

claim: Activation or maturation of BMSC-derived progeny is probably also involved in the progression of disease.
source: Activation or maturation of BMSC-derived progeny is probably also involved in the progression of disease because accumulation of donor-derived fibroblasts was not observed in syngeneic BMSC transplantation, where fibrosis does not occur.
evidence: The text speculates about this mechanism based on the observation that donor-derived fibroblasts do not accumulate in syngeneic transplantation.

claim: Thy-1+ T-cells isolated from host mice after mismatched BMT were activated by PαS-BMSCs in vitro, as shown by enhanced proliferation and IL-6 secretion.
source: In the mixed lymphocyte reaction experiments, Thy-1+ T-cells isolated from host mice after mismatched BMT were activated by PαS-BMSCs in vitro, as shown by enhanced proliferation and IL-6 secretion.
evidence: The text summarizes this finding from the co-culture experiments shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: The T-cell proliferation was blocked by anti-MHC antibody.
source: In addition, the T-cell proliferation was blocked by anti-MHC antibody.
evidence: The text summarizes this finding from the antibody blocking experiments shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Adoptively transferred T cells from mismatched BMSCs recipients into nude-mice-induced autoimmune-like inflammation and fibrosis in targets organs.
source: Finally, adoptively transferred T cells from mismatched BMSCs recipients into nude-mice-induced autoimmune-like inflammation and fibrosis in targets organs, indicating that autoreactive recipient T cells were activated by antigens presented by MHC class II molecules in minor antigen mismatched donor BMSCs.
